text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Federal Cabinet will next week consider a proposal to allow mining and exploration for minerals in forests protected under the new national reserve system. The plan will be introduced to Cabinet by Primary Industries and Energy Minister John Anderson and Resources Minister Warwick Parer, and has the support of the mining industry, yet has already sparked criticism from the conservation movement. Page 1.

Last year saw 95 billion e-mail messages were sent compared with 85 million letters and an 800 percent rise in the use of the Internet, which poses a serious challenge for network operators, suppliers and customers alike. A change on traditional network plan was necessary because of the complexity of the developing and competitive industry, according to Telstra's Peter Darling, speaking at the Network 96 conference in Sydney this week. Page 2.

ACTU Secretary Bill Kelty has told a Melbourne conference that new "inequitable" Federal industrial laws have intensified the ACTU's campaign to win commitments from individual companies not to cut workers' conditions. Kelty was speaking in response to te Federal Government's Workplace Relations Act, which he claims will not improve industrial relations in Australia. Page 4.

The ACTU yesterday lodged a 'living wage' claim with the Australian Industrial Relations Commission, prompting the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry to suggest a $5-a week special allowance for low paid employees. In a written submission to the National Wage Case, the ACCI has also requested that a single minimum wage at below award rates be created. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following weeks of internal bickering, and a slump in voter support, South Australian Liberal Premier Dean Brown was last night deposed by his long-time rival and Industry Minister John Olsen. The coup saw Olsen elected unopposed, with Brown not standing for leadership after six MPs approached him late yesterday saying they wanted the issue resolved. Industrial Affairs Minister Ingerson was elected Deputy Premier. Page 1.

Indonesian Ambassador Wiryono Sastrohandoyo said yesterday that Prime Minister John Howard must show leadership over his own MPs' fears of Indonesia. As a recent survey showed that 76 percent of Coalition MPs feared Indonesia as a security risk, Wiryono said he classes these MPs among the Australians who "saddened" and "astounded" him. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday threatened an increase in taxes following the blocking in the Senate of A$400 million in Budget cuts to welfare for newly arrived migrants. Costello believes someone must pay for the Senate's rejection of the Buget plan, and that would end up being the Australian taxpayers. Page 1.

Despite a warning from the Privacy Commission that taxation and social security data bases could be too sensitive to be operated commercially, the Federal Government is moving towards a plan to privatise its public service computer network next year. The move has alarmed Australia's computer industry, with the Australian Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association saying A$100 million in public service contracts could be lost. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday warned of economic repercussions after the Senate continued to make changes to Budget legislation. Costello said higher interest rates and increased taxes were not out of the question as the Senate's "vicious nitpicking" had already altered the Budget's bottom line. Page 1.

New Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG) president Olympics Minister Michael Knight is fast becoming the public face of SOCOG, replacing SOCOG chief executive Dr Mal Hemmerling as the committee frontman. Knight, rather than the usual Hemmerling, did media interviews at the recent International Olympic Committee meeting in Mexico, and he also met with IOC President Juan Antonio Samaranch. Page 1.

It has been revealed that inaccurate mining maps issued by the Department of Minerals Resources may have contributed to the accident that killed four men in the Gretley Mine disaster. The revelation has prompted a call by the New South Wales Government to order a full judicial inquiry into the deaths. Page 1.

In the latest round of fighting between Sydney councils and telecommunications carriers over aerial cables, a move by the executive of the Local Government Association is expected to be ratified by mayors this morning. The move will see telecommunication carriers charged up to A$300 per subscriber. Page 1.
THE AGE

The National Competition Council has said the Kennett Government's decision to review the scope of the powers of the State auditor-general was not a priority of the national competition agreement, which stipulates that states and territories subject their activities to competition. Page A1.

The Remaking Families: Adaptation of parents and children to divorce report, by Dr Kathleen Funder of the Institute of Family Studies, has found that contrary to popular beliefs, divorce does not leave Australian children emotionally scarred or without a family. The report found children are able to extend their family to include new members beyond the boundaries of households. Page A1.

Reed Consumer Books Australia managing director Adrian Collette looks set to take up the top job in Australia's performing arts industry - the general manager of the Australian Opera. Collette is a former soloist with the Victorian State Opera, and he wold replace Donald McDonald, who became chairman of the ABC in July. Page A1.

Australian armed forces chief General John Baker said yesterday the security of Australia must be reviewed, given changes in strategic circumstances, the end of the Cold War, and the need for the defence forces to adjust. Baker confirmed reports that Defnce Minister Ian McLachlan had ordered a confidential military review into threats from Asia to Australia. Page A1.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
